plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to you; if you bid lower, you risk losing an auction you could have profitably won. Since my value is $49, the maximum possible value, I should bid exactly my true value to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. Since my value is $44, I should bid exactly $44 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $22, I will bid $22 to maximize expected profit.
